criteria.evidence: The test a_critic_revise_sends_the_next_planner_call_at_the_revision_model_and_effort passed (1 passed). It goes through athena.ask and then athena.go with a FakeAgentDriver script. It checks the agent specs, the Planner invocation records [(haiku, high), (sonnet, xhigh)] and the two planner UI lines. Athena's fails-without-1 run shows it fails (exit 101) when planning.rs and config.rs are reverted. I used the release profile because the debug target dir held a stale athena-data artifact from that fails-without run.

criteria.criterion: New tests show that a mechanical plan-rule revision also escalates the next planner call. They also show that a key weaker than the current planner model or effort is ignored, and that with both keys unset every round keeps the same model and effort. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

summary: The change does what the request and the accepted reading ask. Two new optional [models] keys, planner_revision_model and planner_revision_effort, are added. Models::planner_revision_setting applies them part by part, only when a part is set and not weaker than the current value: effort is ranked by its place in EFFORT_LEVELS, and the model by its place in producer_allowed, weakest first. planning_round uses them only when `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`, so round 1 and a seeded first call keep the ordinary setting. The code does not read hard_producer_* or producer_setting. The planner line now shows the effort, and the invocation record carries both model and effort. I ran every new test and all of them pass: the 4 core tests through Athena::go, the 6 athena-data config tests, and the drain.rs test against the real athena.toml. The existing roles_without_* family tests still pass. Athena's fails-without runs show the core tests and the config tests fail when the fix is reverted. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded CI run. The CHANGELOG, D179 and spec.toml claims match the code I read in reading.rs (producer_setting) and run/mod.rs (planning mode); the D179 diff only adds lines. Only files on the deliverables list changed. One note about the environment, not the change: the shared debug target dir held a stale athena-data library left by Athena's fails-without run, so `cargo test -p athena-core` in debug failed to compile with "no method planner_revision_setting". The source does define that method (config.rs:377), and CI passed on this commit. I ran the core and drain tests with `--release` so everything was rebuilt from the current sources.
